out.role: Houston's third receiver behind Nico Collins

doFirst.why: Wilson is rostered in 85.8% of leagues and is a free agent here. That is the largest standing error on either wire and the most valuable thing a wire can hold — someone in this league let a starting receiver go. PFF has him stepping into Arizona's WR1 role this week. Read the status field before you act: he is a FREE AGENT, not a waiver claim, so he costs you nothing. That distinction matters more here than anywhere else, because IPADE's waiver order never resets and you sit fifth — a claim would drop you to tenth for the rest of the season. This one does not. He is not a Week 1 start: Arizona draws the Chargers, the No. 4 defence this week. Boutte leaves because he is 15.9% rostered and third in Houston's receiver room. The deadline is Houston's 17:00 kickoff, not Arizona's 20:25 — Boutte locks first and a locked player cannot be dropped.

action.label: Add Michael Wilson, drop Kayshon Boutte

trades.headline: Team 13's second quarterback scores them nothing every week. Golden is worth a real +1.2 to them, and he is the piece you can lose without touching a starting slot.
trades.yourSurplus: Golden is outside your best lineup — Garrett Wilson and Rice hold the receiver slots and the flex goes to a running back — so trading him costs you zero points this week. He is a genuine asset, not a throwaway, which is why this offer stands a chance of being accepted.
trades.theirHole: Lamar Jackson (18.1) sits on their bench behind Josh Allen (18.5) in a one-quarterback league and cannot score for them all season. Their flex is Travis Kelce at 9.8.
trades.yourLineup: Lamar replaces Stafford at quarterback for +1.5, and that understates it — Stafford already gave you 4.1 this week in a slot you could not move, and Lawrence at 16.0 is the ceiling of your QB room otherwise.
trades.theirLineup: Golden (11.0) takes Kelce's (9.8) flex seat for +1.2, and they still start Josh Allen at quarterback. Nothing they actually use gets worse.
trades.risk: Golden is a second-year receiver whose role is still growing in a crowded Green Bay passing game, so you may be selling before the price peaks — if he breaks out, this looks bad in November. Take that risk anyway: a quarterback you can never start is worth less than one who starts every week. If they accept, drop Stafford; you do not need three quarterbacks. The honest limitation: both gains are one-week numbers, because only weekly projections are published, and season-long is the right unit for a trade. Season-long, a WR4 for a top-two fantasy quarterback is a larger win than +1.5 suggests.

candidates.note: Ignore the rank. Travis Hunter carries an analyst-consensus rank of 1 in this file against a 5.6 projection, and the projection is the one telling the truth: Liam Coen has him taking more work at cornerback than receiver, and Jacksonville's official Week 1 depth chart lists him second at right wide receiver behind Brian Thomas Jr., which puts him roughly fourth in the route order behind Thomas, Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington. Maye-day dropping him on the 9th was correct, not a blunder, and he is 65.7% rostered here because the rest of the league has not looked past the label. This row exists so you skip him rather than wonder why a rank-1 player is free.

Jayden Reed is rostered in 70.7% of leagues and free here. He is Green Bay's most established receiver, and with Josh Jacobs unavailable the offence will lean on the pass more than it planned to. If you make the Lamar trade and send Golden out, Reed is the receiver to replace him with — same offence, more established role, and he is a free agent, so replacing Golden costs you nothing and no waiver priority in a league where priority never resets.

Quentin Johnston is rostered in 75.0% of leagues and free here — Los Angeles' outside receiver opposite Ladd McConkey. Read his 10.4 with care: Arizona is the lowest-ranked defence in the league this week, so that number is matchup, not role. Worth watching to see whether the role holds up against someone competent.

Jordan Mason is rostered in 68.1% of leagues and free here — Minnesota's short-yardage and early-down back. He matters only because your running back depth behind Taylor, Barkley, Tuten and Lloyd thins out fast, and because Lloyd's entire workload rests on Josh Jacobs being on the Commissioner's Exempt List, which can be lifted without warning. Free agent, so no waiver cost and no rush.
